An adult veilwalker is about the size of a dining table, but only knee-high. It has no head, no central mouth, and no obvious front. Its body resembles a shallow, six-sided bowl turned upside down, supported by six flexible limbs.

The veilwalker carries much of its food supply with it.

Its membranes house colonies of microscopic organisms that harvest the star’s reddish light. These symbionts give the unfolded veil its almost black, burgundy color and supply their host with sugars. In return, the veilwalker provides minerals, moisture, and protection.

Young grazers lack this glow. They acquire the luminous organisms by rubbing against adults, often spending several days tucked beneath the overhanging edge of a parent’s body.

The grazer has no eyes that form pictures.
